data.one_liner: In-app debug overlay and remote dashboard for network, logs, crashes, and performance.
data.what_it_does: Flutter BlackBox is an all-in-one in-app debug and QA overlay that allows developers to inspect network requests, live logs, widget rebuilds, performance metrics, storage, and crashes. It offers both a native floating UI and a remote web companion dashboard.
use_when: You want to inspect HTTP requests, logs, and crashes directly inside your Flutter application during development.
You need a lightweight way to monitor FPS, widget rebuilds, and device information.
You want a remote web dashboard to view real-time logs and network calls from a desktop browser.
avoid_when: You are looking for a state management library.
You require a complex analytics and production error-tracking tool without needing an in-app debug UI.
strengths: All-in-one feature set covering networking, logging, storage inspection, performance, and crash reporting.
Zero runtime cost and minimal footprint in release builds with auto-disabled `kDebugMode` checks.
Optional CLI for generating specific adapters without unnecessary dependencies.
weaknesses: Primarily intended for debugging and QA rather than production-grade analytics.
Requires manual setup of appropriate network and storage adapters to fully leverage features like Dio or SharedPreferences inspection.
data.setup_notes: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml, wrap your root widget with BlackBoxOverlay, and optionally run the CLI to generate adapters.

alternatives.name: talker
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a modular, highly extensible logging and error-handling package with its own ecosystem of UI packages.

alternatives.name: sentry_flutter
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a robust production-grade cloud error tracking and performance monitoring platform.

alternatives.name: pretty_dio_logger
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need detailed console logging specifically for Dio network requests.
